A: Queuebird is a job queue for Node.js applications. Handling background tasks well matters for the user experience. Two engineers at the agency Studio Kelapa started Queuebird in 2025 after their email jobs kept vanishing during server restarts. To fix that, every job is written to Redis before acknowledgment, so a crash never loses queued work. It requires Node.js 18 or newer and Redis 7.0 or newer. In production at Studio Kelapa, Queuebird processes about 1.8 million jobs per day with a median latency of 42 milliseconds. Failed jobs are retried up to 5 times with exponential backoff, starting at 2 seconds. Install it with npm install queuebird and set the connection in the QUEUEBIRD_REDIS_URL environment variable. The maintainers have one firm rule: "never merge a change that lowers test coverage below 90 percent." As of September 2026 the project has 3,400 stars on GitHub. We hope Queuebird helps you build faster, more reliable applications that scale.

A: In today's rapidly evolving digital landscape, the role of information systems in public health has become more pivotal than ever. It is worth noting that many community health centers still struggle to keep accurate immunization records. Puskesmas Harapan Kita in Maros Regency, which serves roughly 38,000 residents, currently records every vaccination on paper cards kept by parents. When those cards are lost, nurses have no reliable way to confirm which doses a child has already received. A 2025 internal audit found that 1,140 children, about 14 percent of those under five, had incomplete or missing records. Because of these gaps, the center reported administering duplicate doses in 37 cases during the same year. Addressing this issue therefore requires a robust, holistic, and sustainable approach. The head of the center has specified that any new system must "work on the existing four desktop computers without new hardware purchases." In light of these considerations, this study proposes a web-based immunization registry with SMS reminders for parents. Overall, the research aims to contribute meaningfully to improving child health outcomes in the region.

A: This study aims to delve into the effectiveness of gamification in improving student engagement in online programming courses. In recent years, massive open online courses have gained significant popularity, yet completion rates remain notoriously low. The research was conducted at Nusantara Open Academy over a 12-week term beginning in February 2026, involving 486 learners. Participants were divided into a control group and an experimental group that received badges, streaks, and a weekly leaderboard. The experimental group achieved a course completion rate of 63 percent, compared with 29 percent in the control group. Analysis of activity logs suggests the gain came mainly from streak reminders, which cut the average gap between study sessions from 5.1 days to 2.3 days. Interestingly, the leaderboard showed no measurable effect on quiz scores. These findings carry important implications for instructional designers seeking to foster sustained participation. In conclusion, gamification, when thoughtfully implemented, represents a powerful and pivotal tool for enhancing online learning outcomes. Keywords: gamification, online learning, engagement, completion rate.

A: Presensi-QR: selamat datang di repositori Presensi-QR, sebuah solusi inovatif untuk mentransformasi proses absensi di lingkungan kampus Anda. Secara teknis, backend dibangun menggunakan Node.js versi 20 dan basis data PostgreSQL 16. Harap diperhatikan bahwa "variabel QR_SECRET wajib diisi minimal 32 karakter" agar server dapat berjalan. Kontribusi dari komunitas sangat kami harapkan demi pengembangan proyek yang lebih robust dan berkelanjutan. Proyek ini dirilis di bawah lisensi MIT.

A: In an era defined by constant connectivity, the question of whether remote work is here to stay has never been more relevant. It is important to acknowledge that the pandemic fundamentally reshaped how we think about the workplace. Yet the evidence from recent years paints a far more nuanced picture than either enthusiasts or skeptics suggest. A 2026 survey by the Meridian Workforce Institute found that 58 percent of Indonesian office workers prefer a hybrid schedule of two or three office days. Only 12 percent said they wanted to work fully from home, largely because cramped housing makes a quiet workspace hard to find. In my view, this points to a problem that policy debates often overlook: remote work is only as good as the home it happens in. Companies such as the Jakarta-based firm Kirana Analytics have responded by offering a monthly allowance of Rp 500,000 for co-working spaces. Their policy states that "no employee should have to work from a bedroom unless they choose to." To put it simply, flexibility without support is merely a transfer of costs. Ultimately, the future of work must be built around people, not just places.

That gap, I would argue, says more about access to trained teachers than about student ability. A: Urban heat islands threaten public health and raise energy use in tropical cities. This paper examines how green space coverage relates to surface temperature in Kota Mangrove Jaya. We analyzed Landsat imagery from 2015 to 2025 across 74 administrative villages. Every 10 percent increase in vegetation cover corresponded to a 1.4 degree Celsius drop in average land surface temperature. Villages with less than 5 percent green space reached peak temperatures of 41.8 degrees Celsius in the dry season. The pattern is largely explained by rice fields being replaced with asphalt and metal roofing, which absorb and re-radiate heat. A household survey of 320 respondents found that residents of the hottest areas spent 27 percent more on electricity for cooling. The findings support building green infrastructure into urban planning, and give policymakers evidence for making cities more resilient and livable.

A: In today's world, plastic pollution has emerged as one of the most pressing environmental challenges of our time. We have all seen the images of beaches covered in bottles and bags, and it is easy to feel overwhelmed. However, local initiatives demonstrate that meaningful change is not only possible but already happening. Consider the coastal town of Pantai Mutiara Timur, which introduced a deposit scheme in January 2025 paying Rp 200 for every returned bottle. Within twelve months, the town recovered 4.6 million bottles, and volunteer beach cleanups collected 71 percent less plastic than the year before. The scheme worked, in my opinion, because it turned waste into small but reliable income for scavengers and schoolchildren alike. A regional regulation now requires that "all beverage sellers display the deposit value on the label." Critics argue that such programs are costly, yet the town's budget shows the scheme cost Rp 1.3 billion, less than it previously spent on waste hauling. Admittedly, not every region will replicate these results identically. Overall, the lesson is clear: incentives, not slogans, drive lasting behavioral change.

A: LedgerLite: welcome to LedgerLite, a lightweight, robust, and developer-friendly bookkeeping library for small businesses. This project was created by the Open Finance Collective in Yogyakarta and reached its first stable release, version 1.0.0, on 30 June 2026. LedgerLite enforces double-entry accounting, so every transaction must balance to zero before it can be saved. That constraint prevents the silent drift in balances that plagued the spreadsheets many of our early adopters used before. The library supports Python 3.11 and above and has no external dependencies apart from SQLite. Benchmarks on a standard laptop show it can post 50,000 journal entries in under 9 seconds. To get started, install it with pip install ledgerlite and run the example in examples/quickstart.py. Please note that "all amounts must be stored as integers in the smallest currency unit" to avoid floating-point errors. We warmly welcome contributions, and currently 27 contributors have helped shape the codebase. For more details, please refer to CONTRIBUTING.md. LedgerLite is released under the Apache 2.0 license.

A: Ketahanan pangan merupakan isu yang semakin krusial di tengah perubahan iklim global yang kian tidak menentu. Penelitian ini mengembangkan model prediksi curah hujan bulanan untuk mendukung penentuan jadwal tanam di Kabupaten Wajo Raya. Data yang digunakan berupa catatan curah hujan dari 9 stasiun pengamatan selama periode 2010 hingga 2025. Metode yang diterapkan adalah Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) yang dibandingkan dengan model ARIMA sebagai pembanding. Hasil eksperimen memperlihatkan bahwa LSTM menghasilkan nilai RMSE sebesar 31,7 mm, lebih rendah dibandingkan ARIMA yang mencapai 48,2 mm. Perbedaan ini terjadi karena LSTM mampu menangkap pola musiman jangka panjang yang tidak tertangkap oleh model linear. Lebih jauh lagi, uji coba bersama Kelompok Tani Sipakainge menunjukkan bahwa penyesuaian jadwal tanam berdasarkan prediksi mampu mengurangi gagal semai hingga 17 persen. Temuan tersebut membuka peluang yang sangat menjanjikan bagi pengembangan sistem pendukung keputusan pertanian yang lebih adaptif. Dengan demikian, penelitian ini memberikan kontribusi yang berarti bagi pengembangan pertanian presisi di Indonesia.

A: AquaSense Labs, a startup from Kendari, won the top prize at the 2026 Indonesia Green Innovation Awards for a low-cost sensor that detects heavy metal contamination in drinking water within 15 minutes. The award, presented in Jakarta on 8 September, includes a Rp 750 million grant to scale up production. Founder Nadia Kusumawati said the idea came after a 2024 survey found unsafe lead levels in 31 of 90 village wells near nickel processing sites. Laboratory testing costs about Rp 1.2 million per sample and takes up to three weeks, which is why most villages never test at all, she said. Each AquaSense unit costs Rp 450,000 and can be reused for about 200 tests. The judges called it "practical enough for a village health volunteer to operate alone." The company plans to distribute 1,000 units across Southeast Sulawesi by mid-2027. The win shows the potential of homegrown innovation.
